ky_tectonic_wall.blurb: Tectonic Wall is a mid-sized cliff in Muir Valley, in the Red River Gorge near Rogers. It holds fourteen routes, mostly bolted lines with six traditional ones mixed in, and the grades run from about 5.7 up to 5.12, with 5.10 the clear centre of gravity. That makes it a good stop for climbers who want sustained, pumpy moderates rather than a warm-up wall. The face tends to sit in shade, which keeps the stone cool on mild days, and the lines are roughly 55 to 80 feet tall. It sits around the corner from Johnny's Wall, so the two are easy to combine in one visit.

ky_1_buckeye_buttress.blurb: Buckeye Buttress is the leftmost sector of the Motherlode, a steep, demanding part of the Red River Gorge. Thirteen of its fourteen routes are bolted and one is traditional. The grades start near 5.9 and top out in the low 5.13s, but the bulk of the wall is 5.12, so it suits climbers who are already comfortable on hard sport routes. The rock is slightly overhanging and technical, with a few warm-ups and some bouldery classics. It picks up early sun, which makes it pleasant on cool autumn mornings. Expect to share the trail with others heading to the rest of the Motherlode.

ky_big_wall.blurb: Big Wall is a small bouldering spot inside Cherokee Park in Louisville, a rock wall you can spot from the parking lots where Beargrass Road meets Alta Vista Road. It offers fourteen problems on the park's limestone, including a few short traverses across the wall and a perch. Most of the climbing is easy to moderate: about half sits at V0 or below, a similar number at V2, and just one or two harder lines near V5. It is an urban, low-key session that suits beginners, kids and anyone wanting a quick after-work spot rather than a destination day.

ky_east_coast_crag.blurb: East Coast Crag is a small wall in the Cathedral Domain climbing area, in the Red River Gorge. It has fourteen routes, mostly sport with a few traditional lines, and almost all of them are moderate: a handful run from about 5.5 to 5.9, while 5.10 is the most common grade. The style is technical and close to vertical, and the wall catches morning sun. Reaching it takes a hike of roughly twenty minutes with plenty of ups and downs, so it works best as a quiet half-day for climbers who prefer easier grades over the gorge's steeper, harder walls.

ky_morgue_the.blurb: The Morgue is a compact crag at Miller Fork in the Red River Gorge, with fourteen routes: twelve bolted and two traditional. It is a hard wall. Every line is 5.10 or harder, and roughly two thirds are 5.12 and 5.13, so it is aimed at strong sport climbers. The rock is streaked and golden, with crimpy, juggy lines that locals rate among the better stone at Miller Fork. The wall sees sun for most of the day, which suits fall, winter and spring, although tree cover makes summer visits possible. It is a short walk beyond the Graveyard sector.
